intended_object: For a continuous homomorphism f : G → H of topological groups, f sends the k-th term λ_k of the (closed) p-lower central series into the corresponding term for H, so it induces a homomorphism gr_k(G) = λ_k(G)/λ_{k+1}(G) → gr_k(H) on the graded pieces. Inferred from the docstring and the library's definition of `gradedPiece`.
explanation: `gradedPiece p G k` is defined as `Additive (λ_k ⧸ λ_{k+1}.subgroupOf λ_k)`. The definition restricts f to λ_k(G), co-restricts it to λ_k(H) using `map_pLowerCentralSeries_le`, and applies `QuotientGroup.map`. The compatibility condition uses the same lemma at k+1 to check that λ_{k+1}(G) lands in λ_{k+1}(H). The result is then turned into an additive homomorphism with `MonoidHom.toAdditive`. So it is exactly the map induced on the quotients λ_k/λ_{k+1}, which is the standard functoriality of the associated graded. Continuity is needed because the terms of the series are closures, so this is the natural setting. Mathlib has no p-lower central series of topological groups and no graded map for one.
